Anik Milk Products Private Limited vs Suresh Kumar Agarwal 
And Ors on 10 September, 2024
Ocdsl-1
 Order  SHEET  IP-COM/27/2024  IA No. GA-COM/1/2024  IN THE HIGH COURT AT CALCUTTA  COMMERCIAL DIVISION  ORIGINAL SIDE  ANIK MILK PRODUCTS PRIVATE LIMITED  Vs  SURESH KUMAR AGARWAL AND ORS  BEFORE:
 The Hon'ble JUSTICE KRISHNA RAO  Date : September 10, 2024. 
 Appearance:
 Mr. Soumya Ray Chowdhury, Adv.
 Ms. Susrea Mitra, Adv.
 Mr. Amandeep Singh, Adv.
 Mr. Riyanshu Agarwal, Adv.
 Ms. Bhawna Tikrewal, Adv.

 ... for the plaintiff  The Court: Considering the urgency and the prayer made by the counsel for the plaintiff, this Court has allowed the plaintiff to move the suit as unlisted motion. 
 The plaintiff has prayed for leave under Clause 12 of the Letters Patent on the ground that the plaintiff is outside the jurisdiction of this Court but the defendant nos. 1 and 2 are within the jurisdiction of this Court. He submits the defendant no.3 is also outside the jurisdiction of this Court. Counsel for the plaintiff submits that some cause of action arose within the jurisdiction of this Court and some case of action arose outside the jurisdiction of this Court.

1  Considered the submission made by the counsel for the plaintiff. 
Perused the plaint, cause title and the pleadings. This Court finds that sufficient cause has been shown for granting leave under Clause 12 of the Letters Patent. Accordingly, leave under Clause 12 of the Letters Patent is granted. 
 The plaintiff has also prayed for leave under Section 12A of the Commercial Courts Act and submitted that only in the last week of August and in the first week of September, 2024 the plaintiff came to know that the defendant is selling deceptively similar products of the plaintiff, namely,
"Anik Ghee" and as such there is an urgency to file the an application and also to move an application praying for ad interim order. Accordingly, the plaintiff has not initiated pre institution mediation process. 
 Considered the submission made by the counsel for the plaintiff and the pleadings. This Court finds that sufficient cause has been shown for not taking the recourse of pre institution mediation process and there is an urgency in the said application. Accordingly, leave under Section 12A of the Commercial Courts Act is granted. 
 The plaintiff has also prayed for leave under Order II Rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Counsel for the plaintiff submits that only when the plaintiff came to know that the defendant is selling the product which is deceptively similar to that of the plaintiff's product and accordingly, the plaintiff immediately filed the suit and there is chance of arising further cause of action in future and as such, leave is prayed for under Order II Rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Heard learned counsel for the  3 plaintiff. Perused the plaint. Leave under Order II Rule 2 of the Code of Civil Anik Milk Products Private Limited vs Suresh Kumar Agarwal And Ors on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169419171/
2 Procedure is granted. 
 Plaint is admitted subject to scrutiny by the department. 
 The plaintiff is allowed to move the application being GA- COM/1/2024 for ad interim order. 
 The plaintiff has filed the present application for grant of ad interim order. 
 In the year 2016 the plaintiff by way of deed of assignment obtained an irrevocable assignment and transfer, together with goodwill of certain trademarks from Anik Industries Limited for valuable consideration. 
 In the year 1965 Hindustan Lever Limited adopted, coined and started using the mark 'ANIK' for selling various dairy products, including but not limited to ghee and milk in Class 29. The plaintiff has made extensive advertisement, marketing and the high quality of the ghee, the product under the mark "ANIK" bearing a unique and distinct get-up,
packaging and colour combination which became extremely popular amongst the customers at large. Due to the continuous, extensive and uninterrupted use as well as the superior quality of the ghee products manufactured, marketed and sold under the mark "ANIK", the mark acquired goodwill and reputation amongst the customers across India,
particularly, in North and East India.
 Anik Industries Limited also applied for registration for several "ANIK" trademarks over the years. The trademarks obtained by the Anik Industries Limited is still valid and subsisting. The plaintiff after obtaining the trademark applied to the Trademark Registry for getting its name  4 registered as a subsequent proprietor of the said trademarks. The mark Anik Milk Products Private Limited vs Suresh Kumar Agarwal And Ors on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169419171/
3 "ANIK" along with a unique get-up, packaging, colour combination was continuously and extensively and uninterruptedly used by the plaintiff through its predecessor-in-title for the last more than five decades. In order to protect its customers from getting deceived and have health issues, the plaintiff employed and authorized dealers in parts of India for distributing and supplying the ghee products. 
 By virtue of extensive, open, continuous and uninterrupted usage of the plaintiff's ghee product bearing the unique and distinct get-up,
colour combination and packaging, trade dress under the trademark "ANIK"
since 1965, the said mark has become inseparably and exclusively associated with the business identity of the plaintiff. 
 The plaintiff's well-known trademark "ANIK" has become a prominent name in the dairy business which is used by the plaintiff as a house mark in respect of well-known and widely accepted products. Due to such prominence of the plaintiff's mark "ANIK" the ghee products bearing the trade dress has also achieved substantial goodwill, reputation and recognition in the market. For the year 2023-24, the total sale turnover of the plaintiff with respect of the Anik ghee is Rs.4,36,66,60,862/-. 
 Learned counsel for the plaintiff submits that the defendant no.1 is carrying business under the name and style Sudha Ghee Deport and is engaged in the business of selling, marketing, distributing, offering to sell or dealing otherwise in spurious dairy product including ghee which are identical and deceptively similar and slavish copy of the products of the plaintiff bearing the trademark "ANIK" and the trade dress. He submits that  5 the defendant no.2 owns, runs, controls, manages and operates and interactive e-commerce website by the name of IndiaMART and the Anik Milk Products Private Limited vs Suresh Kumar Agarwal And Ors on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169419171/
4 defendant no.2 runs, controls, manages and operates and interactive e- commerce Just Dial. 
 Counsel for the plaintiff submits that the defendant nos. 1 to 4 appear to be firms/entities/persons inter alia engaged in the business of manufacturing, selling, marketing, distributing, offering to sell or dealing otherwise in spurious dairy products including the ghee which are identical and deceptively similar and slavish copy of the product of the plaintiff bearing trademark "ANIK" and the trade dress.
 He submits that in the last week of August 2024 the plaintiff came to know from its authorized distributors in Kolkata that the defendants are offering for sale, selling, manufacturing, marketing and otherwise dealing in spurious ghee products identical and deceptively similar trademark and trade dress of the plaintiff. 
 He submits that on conducting further search on or about 29th August, 2024 and 2nd September, 2024 the plaintiff discovered that the defendants infiltrated the mark also through interactive e-commerce website i.e. IndiaMART and Just Dial with the misleading and contradictory information to deceive the customers into purchasing spurious inferior quality ghee products bearing the identical and deceptively similar trademark and the trade dress by giving an impression that those products somehow are connected or associated or originated by the plaintiff. 
 Counsel for the plaintiff submits that the trademark "ANIK" and trade dress of the plaintiff are inherently a distinctive one and the  6 customers will assume that the spurious inferior quality ghee product bearing the identical and deceptively similar trademark and the trade dress Anik Milk Products Private Limited vs Suresh Kumar Agarwal And Ors on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169419171/
5 of the defendant are either an offshoot of the plaintiff's mark or the defendants somehow are associated or connected with the plaintiff or its business.
 Counsel for the plaintiff submits that the act of infringement has been committed by the defendants as the defendants have purportedly used the plaintiff's trademark "ANIK" and trade dress in attempt to imitate authentic trademark/corporate name, domain name of the plaintiff with an intention to escape liabilities, if possible, in such a manner which has caused confusion and/or deception in the mind of public and the members of the trade as regards the source and origin of the goods.
 Counsel for the plaintiff submits that the defendants have no right to use the trademark "ANIK" and the trade dress in any manner whatsoever in respect of their spurious ghee products. He submits that the plaintiff has not permitted nor has granted any licence to the defendants to use the trademark "ANIK" and the trade dress or any other identical or deceptively similar mark and thus, the use of the same is clearly unauthorized, mala fide intention of the defendants to make illegal and wrongful gain from the immense goodwill and reputation gained by the plaintiff for the last more than five decades.
 Heard learned Counsel for the plaintiff. Perused the materials on record. 
 It is found from the record that the following trademarks of the plaintiff are registered:

6  2192011 18/08/2011 31/12/2004 Registered  Class: 29  2. 1281707 18/08/2011 31/12/2004 Registered  Class: 29  3. 2192012 18/08/2011 Registered  Class: 30  4. 1281705 30/04/2004 24/09/1999 Registered  ANIKSPRAY (LABEL)
 Class: 29 The plaintiff has also obtained certificate from the Food Safety and Standard Authority of India under FSS Act, 2006 which is valid upto 27th July, 2025. The plaintiff has also obtained management certificate from the concerned authority with respect of Anik Milk Products Private Limited. The plaintiff has appointed several authorized dealers within the jurisdiction of this Court as well as outside the jurisdiction of this Court with respect of their products. The plaintiff is also using the domain name www.anikdairy.com which is also registered. It is the specific case of the plaintiff that on the last week of August, 2024 the plaintiff came to know that the defendants are selling the deceptively similar product i.e. Anik Ghee of the plaintiff. 
The plaintiff has also produced the original packet of the ghee of the plaintiff and the defendants at the time of hearing of the application. After going through the said packets, this Court finds that the defendants are selling, manufacturing the similar products to that of the plaintiff having the same trade dress as that of the plaintiff. If a person looks at Anik Ghee packets of the plaintiff and the defendants, the only difference will be found that in the packet of the plaintiff's product the weight is mentioned as "Net Quantity : 1 Litre (900 g)" and on the packet of the product of the defendants, it is mentioned as "Net Quantity : 1 Litre (898 g)". After going through the packets of the plaintiff and the defendants, it is found that the defendants have even used the licence number of the plaintiff in the said packet. 
The mark of the plaintiff and the defendants are as follows:
Anik Milk Products Private Limited vs Suresh Kumar Agarwal And Ors on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169419171/
7 PLAINTIFF'S PRODUCT SPURIOUS PRODUCT Considering the above, this Court finds that the trademark "ANIK" and the trade dress of the plaintiff are inherently a distinctive one and the customer will assume that spurious inferior quality of product bearing the identical and deceptively similar and the trade dress of the defendants are either offshoot of the plaintiff's mark or the defendants are associated or connected with the plaintiff or its business. 
It is also found that the act of the defendants shows that it has always been in the complete knowledge of the defendants about the massive and irrefutable market business of the plaintiff for the last several decades respectively plaintiff's unique mark and well known trademark "ANIK" and the trade dress and immense goodwill and reputation attached to the plaintiff. 
In view of the above, this Court finds that the plaintiff has made out a prima facie case and the balance of convenience and inconvenience in favour of the plaintiff. This Court further finds that at this state if an ad interim injunction is not granted and the defendants are allowed to continue to sell/manufacture/produce/marketing Anik Ghee which is deceptively similar to the mark of the plaintiff, the plaintiff will suffer irreparable loss and injury. 
Accordingly, this Court passes an order of injunction restraining the defendants and/or their men,
servants, agents, assigns, stockists, wholesalers, retailers, dealers, subsidiaries, licensees and distributors or any one claiming thereunder or on their behalf from using, manufacturing, selling,
offering to sale, advertising, marketing, and promoting in electronic media or interactive websites or offline markets or otherwise connected with the wrongful acts (including unknowns persons/John Does wherever they may be located in India) and all other persons claiming through or under them or acting on their behalf or under their instructions or acting in concert with them, from committing the tort of passing off their spurious as ghee products bearing the impugned trademarks and trade dress or allied products bearing the mark being "ANIK" , or the trade dress , or under any other mark either in isolation or in conjunction with any other mark which is identical with or deceptively similar to the plaintiff's registered and well-known trademark "ANIK" which also forms an integral part of the plaintiff's domain and brand name in any manner whatsoever till 12th November, 2024. 
This Court finds that the defendants are not only selling Anik Ghee deceptively similar to the mark of the plaintiff but have also used the licence number and address and each of the contents of the packet of the plaintiff except the quantity as mentioned above and as such this is a fit case wherein immediately a Receiver is to be appointed to search the premises, godowns, offices, factories, of the defendant no.1 to 4, their men, servants, agents, assigns, stockists, wholesalers, retailers, dealers,
subsidiaries, licensees and distributors or any one claiming thereunder or on their behalf from using, manufacturing, selling, offering to sell, advertising, marketing, and promoting in electronic media or interactive websites or offline markets of the product having mark "ANIK" or the trade dress as mentioned above.
In view of the above, Mr. Chayan Gupta, is appointed as Receiver to search the premises, godowns,
offices, factories of the defendants and their men, agents and servants and to make inventory of the products, namely, Anik Ghee which is deceptively similar to the mark of the plaintiff.
Anik Milk Products Private Limited vs Suresh Kumar Agarwal And Ors on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169419171/
8 The remuneration of the Receiver is fixed at Rs.2,00,000/- and the plaintiff shall pay the said remuneration to the Receiver. 
The Receiver is directed to submit report before this Court on the next date fixed. 
The interim order passed by this Court shall remain in force till 12th November, 2024. 
The plaintiff is directed to sent the copy of the plaint, application, documents to the defendants and to file affidavit of service on the returnable date. 
List the matter on 12th November, 2024. 
(KRISHNA RAO, J.) RS Anik Milk Products Private Limited vs Suresh Kumar Agarwal And Ors on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169419171/

summary.facts:
The plaintiff has prayed for leave under Clause 12 of the Letters Patent on the ground that the plaintiff is outside the jurisdiction of this Court but the defendant nos. 1 and 2 are within the jurisdiction of this Court.
Accordingly, the plaintiff has not initiated pre institution mediation process.
Accordingly, leave under Section 12A of the Commercial Courts Act is granted.

 The plaintiff has filed the present application for grant of ad interim order.
The trademarks obtained by the Anik Industries Limited is still valid and subsisting.
The plaintiff after obtaining the trademark applied to the Trademark Registry for getting its name  4 registered as a subsequent proprietor of the said trademarks.
The mark Anik Milk Products Private Limited vs Suresh Kumar Agarwal And Ors on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169419171/
3
"ANIK" along with a unique get-up, packaging, colour combination was continuously and extensively and uninterruptedly used by the plaintiff through its predecessor-in-title for the last more than five decades.
In order to protect its customers from getting deceived and have health issues, the plaintiff employed and authorized dealers in parts of India for distributing and supplying the ghee products.

 By virtue of extensive, open, continuous and uninterrupted usage of the plaintiff's ghee product bearing the unique and distinct get-up,
colour combination and packaging, trade dress under the trademark "ANIK"
since 1965, the said mark has become inseparably and exclusively associated with the business identity of the plaintiff.

 The plaintiff's well-known trademark "ANIK" has become a prominent name in the dairy business which is used by the plaintiff as a house mark in respect of well-known and widely accepted products.
Due to such prominence of the plaintiff's mark "ANIK" the ghee products bearing the trade dress has also achieved substantial goodwill, reputation and recognition in the market.
summary.arguments:
Counsel for the plaintiff submits that the trademark "ANIK" and trade dress of the plaintiff are inherently a distinctive one and the  6 customers will assume that the spurious inferior quality ghee product bearing the identical and deceptively similar trademark and the trade dress Anik Milk Products Private Limited vs Suresh Kumar Agarwal And Ors on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169419171/
5 of the defendant are either an offshoot of the plaintiff's mark or the defendants somehow are associated or connected with the plaintiff or its business.
 Counsel for the plaintiff submits that the act of infringement has been committed by the defendants as the defendants have purportedly used the plaintiff's trademark "ANIK" and trade dress in attempt to imitate authentic trademark/corporate name, domain name of the plaintiff with an intention to escape liabilities, if possible, in such a manner which has caused confusion and/or deception in the mind of public and the members of the trade as regards the source and origin of the goods.
 Counsel for the plaintiff submits that the defendants have no right to use the trademark "ANIK" and the trade dress in any manner whatsoever in respect of their spurious ghee products.
He submits that the plaintiff has not permitted nor has granted any licence to the defendants to use the trademark "ANIK" and the trade dress or any other identical or deceptively similar mark and thus, the use of the same is clearly unauthorized, mala fide intention of the defendants to make illegal and wrongful gain from the immense goodwill and reputation gained by the plaintiff for the last more than five decades.

summary.decision:
Accordingly, this Court passes an order of injunction restraining the defendants and/or their men,
servants, agents, assigns, stockists, wholesalers, retailers, dealers, subsidiaries, licensees and distributors or any one claiming thereunder or on their behalf from using, manufacturing, selling,
offering to sale, advertising, marketing, and promoting in electronic media or interactive websites or offline markets or otherwise connected with the wrongful acts (including unknowns persons/John Does wherever they may be located in India) and all other persons claiming through or under them or acting on their behalf or under their instructions or acting in concert with them, from committing the tort of passing off their spurious as ghee products bearing the impugned trademarks and trade dress or allied products bearing the mark being "ANIK" , or the trade dress , or under any other mark either in isolation or in conjunction with any other mark which is identical with or deceptively similar to the plaintiff's registered and well-known trademark "ANIK" which also forms an integral part of the plaintiff's domain and brand name in any manner whatsoever till 12th November, 2024.

This Court finds that the defendants are not only selling Anik Ghee deceptively similar to the mark of the plaintiff but have also used the licence number and address and each of the contents of the packet of the plaintiff except the quantity as mentioned above and as such this is a fit case wherein immediately a Receiver is to be appointed to search the premises, godowns, offices, factories, of the defendant no.1 to 4, their men, servants, agents, assigns, stockists, wholesalers, retailers, dealers,
subsidiaries, licensees and distributors or any one claiming thereunder or on their behalf from using, manufacturing, selling, offering to sell, advertising, marketing, and promoting in electronic media or interactive websites or offline markets of the product having mark "ANIK" or the trade dress as mentioned above.
In view of the above, Mr. Chayan Gupta, is appointed as Receiver to search the premises, godowns,
offices, factories of the defendants and their men, agents and servants and to make inventory of the products, namely, Anik Ghee which is deceptively similar to the mark of the plaintiff.
